issues.description: The problem statement and template refer to an interface named 'Milkable' (UML and task text require messageOnMilk() in Milkable). However, the solution implements and uses an interface named 'Dairy' (Dairy.java) and its classes (Goat, Seal) implement Dairy instead of Milkable. Additionally, there is an empty Milkable.java file in the solution repository. This name/type mismatch between 'Milkable' and 'Dairy' is a structural inconsistency that will confuse students and break compilation/tests that expect a 'Milkable' interface.
issues.suggested_fix: Unify the interface name across artifacts. Either rename the solution's Dairy.java (and the interface inside it) to Milkable and have Goat and Seal implement Milkable, or create a proper Milkable interface (with messageOnMilk()) and have the solution classes implement it (remove/replace Dairy). Also remove the unused/empty Milkable.java file or ensure it contains the correct interface. This will align the solution with the problem statement and template.

issues.description: The problem statement and template refer to a 'Milkable' interface (the UML and example Main use Milkable and messageOnMilk()), but the solution implementation defines and uses an interface named 'Dairy' instead. Goat and Seal implement 'Dairy' in the solution while the problem and template expect 'Milkable'. This naming mismatch for the same conceptual entity (the interface that provides messageOnMilk()) creates mapping confusion: students following the instructions to create a Milkable interface will not find the corresponding type in the solution, and comparing solution and template will require an extra mental mapping between 'Milkable' and 'Dairy'.
issues.suggested_fix: Unify the interface name across artifacts. Prefer renaming the solution 'Dairy' interface to 'Milkable' (and update Goat.java and Seal.java to implement Milkable) so it matches the UML and template. Alternatively, if 'Dairy' is preferred, update the problem statement and template (Main) to refer to 'Dairy' instead of 'Milkable'. The first option (rename Dairy -> Milkable in solution) preserves the written exercise and minimizes student confusion.
